documents.title: Gastroenterology consultation
documents.author: gastroenterology
documents.body:
OUTSIDE GASTROENTEROLOGY - new patient consultation. Date of service 08/09/2024.

Referred by his PCP for dysphagia.

HPI: 70 year old man with inclusion body myositis and an aortic aneurysm treated by EVAR. Three months of worsening swallowing. Initially only solid foods, now some liquids as well. Food feels like it lodges in the middle of the chest after he swallows. He has lost 10 pounds without trying over the past two months. Occasional pain behind the breastbone.

PMH: hypertension, GERD on omeprazole, type 2 diabetes, permanent AF on warfarin, prior mild stroke, hyperlipidemia, PAD, AAA s/p EVAR 2022 with cholesterol embolism, IBM.
Medications: metformin, lisinopril, hydrochlorothiazide, metoprolol succinate, warfarin, aspirin, atorvastatin, omeprazole 20 mg. NKDA.
Social: 40 pack-year former smoker; social alcohol.
Family: father with ruptured AAA; mother with diabetes; paternal uncle with Waldenstrom macroglobulinemia.

Exam: weight 78 kg. Appears cachectic. No cervical or supraclavicular lymphadenopathy. Abdomen soft, no organomegaly.

Labs: recent blood work unremarkable.

Assessment: progressive dysphagia to solids then liquids, mid-chest, with weight loss in a former heavy smoker with longstanding reflux - concerning for an obstructing esophageal lesion.
Plan: upper endoscopy with biopsies next week (8/16). Warfarin hold coordinated with his PCP's office. Soft/liquid diet until then.

documents.title: Warfarin hold for EGD
documents.author: RN
documents.body: GI wants warfarin held 5 days before EGD with biopsy 8/16. Last dose was 8/10; hold 8/11 through 8/15. Pt confirmed. No bridging. Restart per GI after the procedure. Keep aspirin.

documents.title: EGD report
documents.author: gastroenterology
documents.body:
OUTSIDE ENDOSCOPY REPORT. Date 08/16/2024.
Procedure: esophagogastroduodenoscopy with biopsies. Moderate sedation.
Indication: dysphagia, weight loss.
Findings:
- Distal esophagus: circumferential ulcerated mass; the standard adult scope was passed through with gentle pressure. Multiple biopsies taken.
- Stomach: normal.
- Duodenum: normal.
Impression: distal esophageal mass, suspicious for malignancy. Biopsies pending.
Plan: resume warfarin tomorrow. Full liquid diet advancing to soft. We will call with pathology and arrange staging. Copy to PCP.

conditions.label: Malignant neoplasm of lower third of esophagus

reports.text:
SPECIMEN: Esophagus, distal, mass, endoscopic biopsies.
MICROSCOPIC: Fragments of glandular mucosa infiltrated by malignant glands with moderate differentiation, invading the lamina propria in the biopsy fragments.
reports.conclusion: Invasive adenocarcinoma, moderately differentiated, distal esophagus.

documents.title: Esophageal cancer diagnosis
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Called pt - GI had already told him yesterday that the biopsy shows adenocarcinoma of the lower esophagus. Went over what happens next: staging scans (CT this coming Monday, PET later next week), ultrasound endoscopy, then the cancer center to plan treatment. He asked good questions. Swallowing liquids and soft food ok, shakes 2-3 a day. Restarted warfarin 8/17, INR at the cancer center labs or here, either is fine. Told him to call me any time.

reports.text:
EXAM: CT chest with IV contrast.
INDICATION: Newly diagnosed distal esophageal adenocarcinoma, staging.
FINDINGS: Circumferential wall thickening of the distal esophagus. No enlarged mediastinal, hilar or paraesophageal lymph nodes. No pulmonary nodules. No pleural effusion.
reports.conclusion: Distal esophageal wall thickening corresponding to known tumor. No thoracic adenopathy or metastasis.

reports.study: CT abdomen and pelvis with contrast
reports.text:
EXAM: CT abdomen and pelvis with IV contrast.
INDICATION: Esophageal cancer staging.
FINDINGS: No gastrohepatic or celiac adenopathy. Liver without focal lesion. Adrenal glands normal. Kidneys enhance symmetrically, no hydronephrosis. Bifurcated aortic endograft in place, aneurysm sac 4.8 cm. No ascites or peritoneal disease.
reports.conclusion: No evidence of abdominal or pelvic metastatic disease. Stable post-EVAR appearance.

documents.title: EUS report
documents.author: gastroenterology
documents.body:
OUTSIDE ENDOSCOPIC ULTRASOUND. Date 09/03/2024.
Indication: staging of distal esophageal adenocarcinoma.
Findings: hypoechoic circumferential mass of the distal esophagus extending through the muscularis propria into the adventitia. No malignant-appearing periesophageal or celiac lymph nodes.
Impression: uT3 N0.
Warfarin was not held (no FNA planned or performed).

medications.sig: Dissolve 1 tablet on the tongue every 8 hours as needed for nausea

documents.title: Oncology consultation - esophageal cancer
documents.author: oncology
documents.body:
OUTSIDE CANCER CENTER - medical and radiation oncology consultation. Date of service 09/05/2024.

Diagnosis: adenocarcinoma of the distal esophagus, moderately differentiated.
Staging: CT chest/abdomen/pelvis 8/26 - distal esophageal thickening, no adenopathy or metastasis. PET-CT 8/29 - avid distal esophageal primary, no other avid disease. EUS 9/3 - uT3 N0. Clinical stage cT3 N0 M0.

Relevant history: inclusion body myositis with proximal and distal weakness, permanent AF on warfarin, prior stroke, diabetes, hypertension, PAD, EVAR 2022 complicated by cholesterol embolism. Weight 78 kg, down about 10 lb.

Discussed at multidisciplinary tumor board. Options were chemoradiation followed by esophagectomy, or definitive chemoradiation. Given his age, IBM-related weakness and vascular comorbidity, the board and Mr. Rossi favored definitive chemoradiation with close surveillance.

Plan:
- Weekly carboplatin AUC 2 and paclitaxel 50 mg/m2 with radiation 50.4 Gy in 28 fractions, starting 9/16.
- Ondansetron 4 mg ODT as needed for nausea.
- Dietitian; high-calorie shakes. Feeding tube only if he cannot keep weight up.
- Weekly CBC during treatment; INR more often while on chemotherapy - his PCP's office manages warfarin and will continue.
- Restaging PET-CT and endoscopy about 3 months after completion.

procedures.procedure: Office visit, established patient, high MDM

documents.title: Office visit - pre-treatment
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Here to go over the cancer plan and sort out his medicines before chemoradiation starts 9/16.

Distal esophageal adenocarcinoma, cT3 N0 M0. Definitive chemoradiation: weekly carboplatin/paclitaxel with 28 radiation treatments.

Swallowing: soft foods and liquids, 2-3 shakes a day. Pills going down if taken one at a time with plenty of water. Wt 76.2 kg.

Exam: thin. Heart irreg irreg. Lungs clear. Abdomen soft.

A/P:
1. Esophageal adenocarcinoma - per oncology. Ondansetron from them.
2. Warfarin during chemo - INR every 1-2 weeks through treatment; RN to coordinate draws with his treatment days. Call with any bleeding.
3. DM2 - eating less; watch for lows. Keep metformin for now, tell us if sugars run under 90 or he can't eat.
4. HTN - BP fine today. If it runs low as weight drops, we will cut back.
5. IBM - stable.
6. Flu shot and covid at the nurse visit in October.
Portal anytime. RTC after treatment.

documents.title: Nurse visit
documents.author: RN
documents.body: Week 4 of chemoradiation. Tired, throat sore with swallowing from the radiation, using the ondansetron a couple times a week. Flu HD and updated covid given (oncology ok'd). INR in range. Next INR in 2 weeks.

documents.title: INR high
documents.author: RN
documents.body: INR 3.3. Eating very little this week, last chemo tomorrow, last radiation Thursday. No bleeding, no black stools, no blood in urine. Per protocol hold tonight's dose then resume 5 mg daily. Recheck at his visit 10/29.

procedures.procedure: Office visit, established patient, moderate MDM

documents.title: Office visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Finished chemoradiation 10/24. Wiped out but improving each day. Swallowing painful the last two weeks of radiation, now easing; soft food and shakes, liquids fine. Nausea gone, hasn't needed ondansetron since last week. No bleeding.

Wt 74 kg (78 at GI in Aug). BP 120s/70s.
Exam: thin, tired. Mouth moist. Heart irreg irreg. Lungs clear. No edema.

Labs: Hgb 11.8 (down during chemo), WBC and platelets ok. Cr stable. A1c 5.7. INR back in range after holding one dose.

A/P:
1. Esophageal adenocarcinoma s/p definitive chemoradiation - restaging in January per oncology. Push calories.
2. Anemia from treatment - expect recovery; recheck CBC next month.
3. DM2 - A1c 5.7 with low intake. No lows. Keep metformin, recheck in the spring.
4. HTN - BP lower with weight loss but not low, no dizziness. Same meds for now.
5. Warfarin - INR every 3-4 weeks again now chemo is done.
RTC 2 months.

documents.title: Oncology end-of-treatment note
documents.author: oncology
documents.body:
OUTSIDE CANCER CENTER - end of treatment visit. Date of service 11/05/2024.
Completed definitive chemoradiation 9/16-10/24/2024 for cT3 N0 M0 adenocarcinoma of the distal esophagus: weekly carboplatin AUC 2 / paclitaxel 50 mg/m2, 50.4 Gy in 28 fractions. All planned treatment delivered.
Toxicity: fatigue, radiation esophagitis now settling, mild treatment-related anemia. Weight nadir 74 kg.
Plan: restaging PET-CT and EGD with biopsies in mid-January. Nutrition follow-up. Ondansetron as needed. Thank you.

reports.text:
EXAM: Duplex ultrasound of the abdominal aorta and endograft.
INDICATION: Surveillance after EVAR 09/2022.
COMPARISON: 10/17/2023.
FINDINGS: Endograft main body and both limbs patent. No endoleak. Aneurysm sac maximal diameter 4.8 cm, unchanged.
reports.conclusion: Stable post-EVAR. Sac 4.8 cm, no endoleak.

documents.title: Vascular surgery surveillance
documents.author: vascular surgery
documents.body:
OUTSIDE VASCULAR SURGERY - EVAR surveillance. Date of service 01/14/2025. Visit delayed from the fall while he was finishing esophageal cancer treatment.
No abdominal or back pain. No leg or toe discoloration.
Duplex: patent graft, no endoleak, sac 4.8 cm, stable.
Plan: annual duplex. Return in 12 months.

documents.title: Oncology restaging visit
documents.author: oncology
documents.body:
OUTSIDE CANCER CENTER - restaging visit. Date of service 01/23/2025.
Distal esophageal adenocarcinoma cT3 N0 M0, s/p definitive chemoradiation completed 10/24/2024.
Restaging: PET-CT 1/13 - no residual FDG avidity at the primary site, no new avid disease. EGD 1/17 - healed mucosa at the treated segment, biopsies negative for malignancy.
Impression: clinical complete response.
He is swallowing normally now and gaining weight back.
Plan: surveillance - CT chest/abdomen every 6 months for 2 years, then yearly; EGD as indicated. Next CT in July. We understand he has new hematuria being evaluated by urology. Thank you.

documents.title: Urology consultation
documents.author: urology
documents.body:
OUTSIDE UROLOGY - new patient consultation. Date of service 02/19/2025.

Referred for hematuria.

HPI: 70 year old man with two months of painless visible blood in the urine and increased urinary frequency. No fever, weight loss or significant pain. On warfarin for AF with a therapeutic INR per his PCP's office.

PMH: esophageal adenocarcinoma treated with chemoradiation, complete response; AAA s/p EVAR; cholesterol embolism 2022; inclusion body myositis; permanent AF; type 2 diabetes; hypertension; hyperlipidemia; PAD; prior mild stroke; GERD.
Medications: hydrochlorothiazide; metformin, lisinopril, metoprolol succinate, warfarin, aspirin, atorvastatin, omeprazole. NKDA.
Social: 40 pack-year history, former smoker.
Family: father ruptured AAA; mother diabetes and macular degeneration; paternal uncle Waldenstrom; brother hypertension.

Vitals: BP 135/85, HR 78.
Exam: abdomen without masses or tenderness. Genitalia normal.

Data: urinalysis today with more than 50 red cells per high-power field, no casts or crystals. Creatinine 1.2 (baseline 1.0), BUN 18. CBC within normal limits. Renal ultrasound 2/4: right hydronephrosis, no stones.

Assessment: painless gross hematuria with right hydronephrosis in a former heavy smoker - urothelial malignancy must be excluded.
Plan: CT urogram, then office cystoscopy. Continue warfarin for now.

documents.title: Office cystoscopy
documents.author: urology
documents.body:
OUTSIDE UROLOGY - flexible cystoscopy. Date 03/04/2025.
Findings: urethra and prostatic urethra unremarkable. Papillary tumor on the right lateral wall obscuring the right ureteral orifice. Left orifice normal with clear efflux. Remainder of the bladder mucosa without lesions.
Plan: transurethral resection of bladder tumor 3/18. Warfarin hold 5 days.

procedures.procedure: Transurethral resection of bladder tumor, large

documents.title: Operative note - TURBT
documents.author: urology
documents.body:
OUTSIDE OPERATIVE NOTE. Date 03/18/2025. Outpatient surgery.
Procedure: cystoscopy, transurethral resection of bladder tumor (about 3 cm), right lateral wall at the right ureteral orifice.
Anesthesia: general.
Findings: papillary tumor on the right lateral wall overlying the right ureteral orifice. Resected completely to visible muscle; deep base biopsies sent separately. Right orifice identified after resection, efflux seen. No other lesions.
EBL minimal. Catheter overnight, removed next morning by visiting nurse.
Plan: resume warfarin 3/20 if urine clear. Pathology review in clinic.

reports.text:
SPECIMENS: A. Bladder tumor, right lateral wall, TURBT. B. Bladder tumor base, deep biopsies.
MICROSCOPIC: A. High-grade papillary urothelial carcinoma with invasion into the lamina propria. B. Detrusor muscle (muscularis propria) present and free of carcinoma.
reports.conclusion: High-grade papillary urothelial carcinoma, invading lamina propria (pT1). Muscularis propria present and not involved.

procedures.procedure: Transurethral resection of bladder tumor, repeat

reports.text:
SPECIMEN: Bladder, right lateral wall, prior resection site, repeat TURBT.
MICROSCOPIC: Urothelial mucosa with cautery and reparative changes. Muscularis propria present. No residual carcinoma.
reports.conclusion: No residual urothelial carcinoma. Muscularis propria present.

documents.title: Operative note - repeat TURBT
documents.author: urology
documents.body:
OUTSIDE OPERATIVE NOTE. Date 04/22/2025.
Procedure: restaging transurethral resection of the prior tumor bed, right lateral wall.
Findings: well-healed resection scar at the right lateral wall, no visible residual tumor; scar and base resected deeply including muscle. Right ureteral orifice with clear efflux. No new lesions.
Plan: resume warfarin in 48 hours. If pathology confirms no residual or muscle invasion, begin BCG induction in 3 weeks.

documents.title: Urology - BCG induction
documents.author: urology
documents.body:
OUTSIDE UROLOGY. Date of service 05/13/2025.
High-grade T1 urothelial carcinoma of the bladder, right lateral wall, s/p TURBT 3/18 and restaging TURBT 4/22 with no residual carcinoma and muscle present.
Plan: intravesical BCG induction, six weekly instillations starting today. First instillation given today, tolerated. Then surveillance cystoscopy in 3 months and maintenance BCG.
Renal ultrasound in June to recheck the right kidney.
